b1-crisisdeuda-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Oil Money and Loans
b1-crisisdeuda-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos watched a documentary about the Latin American debt crisis, and he asks how the banks had so much money to lend.
b1-crisisdeuda-01.prompt: Tell Carlos where the banks got the money and what they did with it.
cues: Say what happened to the oil price in 1973 and name the cause and result
Say where the oil-exporting countries put their money
Say what the banks did with it
b1-crisisdeuda-01.target: A raíz de la subida del petróleo, los países que exportan petróleo depositaron mucho dinero en los bancos, y los bancos otorgaron préstamos a los gobiernos.
b1-crisisdeuda-01.english: As a result of the rise in oil prices, the countries that export oil deposited a lot of money in the banks, and the banks granted loans to the governments.
b1-crisisdeuda-01.canDo: I can say how the oil money of the 1970s ended up in loans to Latin American governments.

b1-crisisdeuda-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What the United States Did in 1979
b1-crisisdeuda-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg read about the debt crisis for a class, and she asks what the United States did in October 1979 and what had already happened in Latin America.
b1-crisisdeuda-02.prompt: Tell Meg what the United States decided in October 1979 and what many countries had already done.
cues: Say what the central bank decided and why
Say what many countries had already done before 1979
b1-crisisdeuda-02.target: En octubre de 1979, el banco central de Estados Unidos decidió elevar las tasas de interés para frenar la inflación. Muchos países ya habían acumulado una deuda grande.
b1-crisisdeuda-02.english: In October 1979, the central bank of the United States decided to raise interest rates to stop inflation. Many countries had already built up a large debt.
b1-crisisdeuda-02.canDo: I can explain what the US Federal Reserve did in October 1979 and why.

b1-crisisdeuda-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The IMF and the Cuts
b1-crisisdeuda-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you learned in a history class about the years after 1982, and he asks what governments did when the banks stopped lending.
b1-crisisdeuda-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what governments did after the banks stopped lending, and what was cut.
cues: Say who many governments turned to
Say what was cut, without saying who cut it
b1-crisisdeuda-03.target: Después de 1982, muchos gobiernos recurrieron al FMI. Se recortó el gasto público.
b1-crisisdeuda-03.english: After 1982, many governments turned to the IMF. Public spending was cut.
b1-crisisdeuda-03.canDo: I can say why governments turned to the IMF after 1982.

b1-crisisdeuda-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Prices and Wages
b1-crisisdeuda-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited an exhibition about the 1980s in Latin America, and she asks what happened to ordinary families.
b1-crisisdeuda-04.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to wages and to work as prices went up.
cues: Say what happened to wages as prices rose
Say what kind of work grew
b1-crisisdeuda-04.target: A medida que los precios subían, los salarios compraban menos, y creció el trabajo informal.
b1-crisisdeuda-04.english: As prices rose, wages bought less, and informal work grew.
b1-crisisdeuda-04.canDo: I can explain how unemployment, informal work and falling wages affected families.

b1-crisisdeuda-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Lost Decade
b1-crisisdeuda-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a book about the 1980s in Latin America, and Carlos asks why people call that decade lost.
b1-crisisdeuda-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what CEPAL called the 1980s and why.
cues: Name the source and what it called the 1980s
Say what happened to income per person
b1-crisisdeuda-05.target: Según la CEPAL, los años ochenta fueron una década perdida, porque en muchos países el ingreso por habitante de 1990 no era mayor que el de 1980.
b1-crisisdeuda-05.english: According to CEPAL, the 1980s were a lost decade, because in many countries income per person in 1990 was not higher than in 1980.
b1-crisisdeuda-05.canDo: I can say what CEPAL called the 1980s and why.

b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Debt Crisis in Order
b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are going over your notes on the debt crisis before a class, and she asks you to tell the main steps in order.
b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg the main steps of the debt crisis in order.
cues: Say what the banks did first
b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.target: Primero, los bancos otorgaron muchos préstamos. Después, en 1982, México anunció que no podía pagar su deuda. En 1989 llegó el Plan Brady.
b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.english: First, the banks granted many loans. Then, in 1982, Mexico announced that it could not pay its debt. In 1989 the Brady Plan came.
b1-crisisdeuda-consolidation.canDo: I can retell the main steps of the debt crisis in order, from the loans of the 1970s to the Brady Plan.
